start: ^Alex's Dad was driving. Occasionally his eyes darted back to Alex in the rear view mirror, probably thinking 'What is going on with that boy?'

b: ^He had no idea what his weird son was thinking about. And Alex could think about whatever he wanted: instead of this bland sunlit street rolling by he could picture a scene from his favourite movie, Lightning on the Moon. He could see a barren island in the Arctic amidst a heaving ocean, where industrious scientists working at the Observatory see for the first time lightning on the moon, and staring at the flicker of light on the dark rocky surface, start to put together what it means.

^Shiny black shoes clung to Alex's feet. Smooth grey trousers, a shirt, tie and blazer confined him in tidy artifice. In the window, Alex saw his own staring eyes, the only thing in this landscape of car and street that was not barren. They were alive.
^'No man is an island.' Alex had heard that somewhere. It wasn't true. Alex's thoughts were completely his own.

start: ^Alex wanted this drive to go on a bit longer. Bland streets rolled by, empty tarmac and waxy box hedges, as he drew inevitably closer to school.
